subject: Re: Creating an order - Encord & Abbvie
text:
Hi William,

Sorry for the delay and Happy New Year.

Good question.

The next step is for you to send the invoice(s) to
invoices@scienceexchange.com. Once we receive them, our team will mark the
order as complete for you.

If the order is marked complete before we receive the invoice, we’re still
able to accept it, but it adds an extra step on our side since we then need
to reach out to the requester for email confirmation before processing.

So sending the invoice first is the smoothest path.

Here are some Help Center article with more information:
https://help.scienceexchange.com/s/article/s-invoice-process
https://help.scienceexchange.com/s/article/s-order-completing-order

Let me know if you have any questions. And sorry again for the delay in
response.

Best,
Cyn

subject: Re: Encord Trial
text:
Hey Zach,

Thanks for the help, I am able to get the tracking/interpolation working with the steps you recommended.

However, this isn’t quite the flow I was expecting. This flow makes sense for annotating the video from scratch, but if you recall we want to start with our pre-annotations. Because our pre-annotations have been loaded such that each frame has its own pose object, im not seeing how to make this work. In addition, is there not a way to set a future key frame (lets say frame 20) and then have the tracking/interpolation occur between those two ground truth key frames? Without the end key frame (the current flow you recommended, places a starting pose (no end pose to reference) and then just let it track in the future) im seeing the tracking/interpolation break down quite quickly once any sort of complex movements start to happen.

If there isn’t a way to do this im not sure Encode will work well for us. Can you please advise on the ideal annotation process for our workflow because right it’s a bit unclear to me.

Thanks,
Max
